source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:21 (the Masorah; Bereshit Rabbah 7)
claim_en: ha-taninim ('the great sea-serpents') is written LEAN in the last yod — the Masorah's note, and BR 7's teaching rides the singular-looking skeleton: this is behemot and leviathan, who have no mates. The lean form stands once in the Torah.
ha-gedolim ('the great ones'): MS notes 'dagesh (the hardening dot) in the gimel' — in-stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:21 (with the Ramah)
claim_en: of kanaf ('winged fowl'): FULL with vav — MS with the Ramah's endorsement, in-stream.
ve-of yeofef ('and fowl that flies', 1:20): 'BOTH written full with vav' — the flying-verb's middle vav checked in-stream (the noun's asserted alongside).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:21 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: 'And every fowl-language in the Torah is likewise FULL' — the rule's negative space verified: the lean skeleton (fowl without its vav) appears ZERO times in the stream, bare or prefixed.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:22 (the Masorah; Chullin 63b)
claim_en: ve-ha-of ('and the fowl') — 'THREE in the Masorah': the fowl shall INCREASE (here), the fowl ATE them (the baker's dream, Gen 40:17), the law of beast and fowl (Lev 11:46) — hinting Chullin 63b: pure birds outnumber the impure. All three stations are Torah-side and the count is EXACT.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:20 (Et Sofer; the Jerusalem-exile books; Rambam)
claim_en: An OPEN paragraph break stands before 'let the waters swarm' — Et Sofer, the precise books of the Jerusalem exile in Spain, and Rambam, against prints that run it on. Paragraph layer uninstrumented in SNAPSHOT — filed as instrument gap.
